sources.quote: At a pressure of one atmosphere (atm), ice melts or water freezes (solidifies) at 0 °C (32 °F) and water boils or vapor condenses at 100 °C (212 °F).

The Sun is a planet..why: Deliberately false so the disjunction turns on the edited property: the Sun is a star.

'Is thrum-keyed to' is symmetric..why: "Thrum-keyed" is a made-up relation (catalogued as thrum_keyed_to, fictional, no property tags): it does not occur in Dolma or on Wikipedia and its words carry no built-in sense of a two-way bond, so a model has no default reading of it as symmetric. A made-up relation has no property to contradict.

notes: RBox expansion paired with physics-replace-0009 (which makes 'decays directly into' symmetric): a made-up relation, thrum_keyed_to, is given the same property, symmetric, applied to real particles. The instance fact is given in each prompt, so the answer is fixed by the edit alone; the pairs (muon and tau, proton and neutron) are not decay pairs and are not linked by any real relation named thrum-keyed, and the name has no built-in two-way or one-way sense. A symmetry insert has no honest 'no' instance, so the first instance asks whether the converse follows (yes) and the second whether it could fail (no); a yes-biased model passes the first only. The side facts and the near and far unrelated queries are those of the revision record (already audited). Cross-lingual prompts keep the coined term untranslated with a directed particle (于, a), so no Chinese or Spanish word for 'link' or 'pair' brings its own symmetry.
